quarterly_data.signal: SCALE-ACROSS PORT MECHANICS (mix itself matches the Q2 call's ~30% of the AI target): VP of Product Line Management Brendan Gibbs said data-center-interconnect scale-across is now 'a third of our business as part of the most recent guide' - the spine becomes geographically dispersed, so customers both re-use high-radix ports with ZR/ZR+ coherent DWDM pluggables AND deploy new platforms. Arista frames scale-across as a win only available to vendors that first won the back-end scale-out cluster.
quarterly_data.figure: scale across now a third of our business

quarterly_data.signal: SUPPLY / DEMAND QUALITY: CFO Chantelle Breithaupt said there is no pull-forward in the order book despite the shortage narrative - 'We don't see pull forward at all... it's 52-week lead time, so I don't think customers are going to lean in to 52 weeks unless they're pretty certain that it's something'. Supply is still not unconstrained going into next year (described as whack-a-mole), and she said that with a bit more supply Arista could beat even the raised FY2026 guide.
quarterly_data.figure: 52-week lead time; we could even go a little higher than the guide

quarterly_data.signal: SCALE-UP ETHERNET (ESAN) SIZING AND POSITION: Gibbs cited an industry analyst report marking Ethernet scale-up networking as high as a $20 billion market by 2030, and said one of Arista's software architects co-chairs the ESAN Network working group at OCP. Breithaupt confirmed Arista has no scale-up product yet ('we do not even have a scale-up offering yet', and none of it sits in deferred revenue), that it will not be material in 2027 financials because standards, pilots and trials come first, and that scale-up will segment into proprietary NVLink, a white-box equivalent, and value-add Ethernet where Arista intends to play.
quarterly_data.figure: a $20 billion market just for Ethernet scale-up networking by 2030; will not be material in our 2027 financials; once it gets going in 2028

quarterly_data.signal: 1.6T TIMING: Gibbs said 1.6T trials are going on now with volume next year, that both air-cooled and liquid-cooled 1.6T systems are announced so liquid cooling is not a gating item (compute nodes drive the liquid-cooling decision, not the network), and that 1.6T ZR optics for scale-across arrive probably next year. Arista is offering XPO (pluggable, liquid-cooled, supports short-range, LPO and ZR+ lasers) alongside open CPO so customers are not locked into one optical approach.
quarterly_data.figure: trials are going on now, volume for next year; 1.6T ZR for scale across probably next year
